articles.title: ScopeGuard: an open-weight model that tells freelancers when "quick one" means "paid one"
articles.excerpt: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 2: Side Hustle Every freelancer knows this message: "Hey! Quick one: could you also add a shop page so we can sell merch? Shoul…
articles.body: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 2: Side Hustle What I Built Every freelancer knows this message: "Hey! Quick one: could you also add a shop page so we can sell merch? Shouldn't take long 🙏" Is a shop page in the contract? You'd have to dig out the statement of work (SOW), find the clause, work out how many hours it is, and then write a reply that says no without souring a client you like. Most of us skip that, say "sure", and do the work for free. Do that a few times a month and it adds up to real money. That's scope creep . ScopeGuard is a small web app that does the awkward part for you: You save a client's SOW and your hourly rate. Paste it in, or import the PDF or Word file the client signed.

articles.body: The GhostAction credential-theft campaign targeted over 30,000 repositories across 3,000 organizations, compromising 1,900 accounts. Attackers used stolen Personal Access Tokens to inject malicious CI/CD automation workflows designed to harvest cloud credentials, registry tokens, and API keys. According to security researchers at GitGuardian, this activity intensified significantly on October 8 and 9, 2026. The attack managed to compromise the accounts of approximately 1.900 users, targeting over 30.000 code repositories across 3.000 users and organizations, while attempting to extract thousands of sensitive data from public projects. How did the attackers act?

articles.title: One release script, two child processes, and only one of them is allowed a shell
articles.excerpt: Notifio ships as desktop installers, so releasing it is a script rather than a deploy. pnpm release bumps the version, builds the installer for whichever OS it is run on, uploads the artifacts to Clou…
articles.body: Notifio ships as desktop installers, so releasing it is a script rather than a deploy. pnpm release bumps the version, builds the installer for whichever OS it is run on, uploads the artifacts to Cloudflare R2, and then asks R2 whether what arrived is the right size. The download page hands out presigned links to those exact objects, which is why a release overwrites a fixed set of keys instead of publishing a new versioned path each time. The script runs two external programs: pnpm , to do the actual building, and aws , to upload. They need opposite treatment, and I got one of them wrong in a way the Node docs now flag. pnpm is not a program On macOS, pnpm is an executable and spawnSync('pnpm', ['build:mac']) works.

Listing Writer turns a product name and a few details (plus an optional photo) into a ready-to-paste title, description and 13 search tags for Etsy or eBay. What I Built Listing Writer is a small web app for people who sell physical products online: Etsy makers, eBay resellers, and people flipping used tech.

articles.title: Statically catching GGUF parser overflow bugs before you load the model
articles.excerpt: I'm MV2, of Munim, Inc. Up front: the tool, the corpus and this post were all made with AI. GGUF, the model container used by llama.cpp, Ollama, LM Studio and PowerInfer, has no code-execution surface…
articles.body: I'm MV2, of Munim, Inc. Up front: the tool, the corpus and this post were all made with AI. The short version GGUF, the model container used by llama.cpp, Ollama, LM Studio and PowerInfer, has no code-execution surface of its own . There is no pickle and no embedded script; nothing "runs" when you open one. But hand-written C/C++ ggml readers and their derivatives have repeatedly turned a malformed header into a heap out-of-bounds write or read through integer overflow. In every one of these bugs, the triggering values live in the file header: a count, a length, a dimension, an offset. So a static pre-load check can read the header and flag the precursor before any loader touches the file. The public cluster Every one of these is already public. Nothing here is a zero-day.

The single most useful habit is this: you almost never have to decide on the call. The two rules that decide how the call goes Thank them, and ask for what you need — details, or time. articles.title: An arrival leaves a link. A reader leaves your words.
articles.excerpt: Last week two new comments landed on a post I wrote. Both were bots. One was an ad for an AI agent product, in Vietnamese, with a link stapled to the bottom. On the dashboard, that's engagement. Two n…
articles.body: Last week two new comments landed on a post I wrote. Both were bots. One was an ad for an AI agent product, in Vietnamese, with a link stapled to the bottom. On the dashboard, that's engagement. Two new comments. The number moved. Nothing else did. I have exactly one comment I'd call a reader. A stranger read the thing, quoted a line of mine back to me, and kept going. No link. No product. Just my sentence, in his mouth, unasked for. I can count the real ones on one hand and I've only been doing this a week. Here's the disease, stated plainly: the metric cannot tell a reader from an arrival. A person who read every word and a bot that pasted a URL ring the doorbell exactly the same way. Views, comments, reactions. They measure whether anyone showed up. Never whether anyone stayed.

articles.title: Fridge hack costing millions and sparking fires stemmed from poor security
articles.excerpt: Incident hitting 700 supermarkets exploited outdated devices exposed to the Internet.
articles.body: Earlier this week, a mass hack of refrigeration systems at an estimated 700 supermarkets throughout France caused them to suddenly malfunction, causing spoilage of untold tons of perishables and, in some cases, fires. As is now the norm, basic cybersecurity would have prevented it. French authorities say the systems, made up of entire fleets of refrigerators and freezers throughout a store, were hacked. More specifically, Internet-connected controllers that allow technicians to remotely administer the store-wide systems were compromised. The unknown attackers responsible then activated defrosters long enough for the fridges to reach temperatures as high as 50° Celsius (122° Fahrenheit).

articles.title: Planetary genealogy: Milky Way worlds belong to 1 of 2 ‘families,’ scientists find
articles.excerpt: Scientists have performed a cosmic genealogy on planetary systems in the Milky Way, finding two distinct families that influence the evolution and fate of these systems.
articles.body: You can tell a lot about how a child will age by looking at their parents, and it turns out that this could be true for planetary systems, too. Scientists have performed cosmic genealogy on planetary systems in the Milky Way, finding two distinct families that influence the evolution and fate of these systems. The study team, led by researchers at the Italian National Institute for Astrophysics (INAF), studied 300 of the best-understood multiplanet systems of the over 1,000 that astronomers have discovered in the Milky Way. The team's research clarifies how the environments around infant stars directly affect planetary fates and, in turn, the survival of extrasolar planets, or exoplanets , that are potentially capable of hosting life.

articles.title: 'Dungeon Crawler Carl' author Matt Dinniman talks inspirations, success, and the upcoming Peacock TV series (interview)
articles.excerpt: 'Luckily I’m still in love with this story, and I am in love with writing it.'
articles.body: Fall has officially arrived, and as autumn leaves blaze in vivid colors, there is no better time to plunge into the imaginative world of New York Times best-selling author Matt Dinniman's "Dungeon Crawler Carl", the wildly addictive science fantasy book series that's taking the world by storm. Even if you haven't read them, you've probably seen folks carrying these books, emblazoned with their loud, neon-colored covers, at your neighborhood coffee house. You'll see it even more in the future, too, as a streaming adaptation of the novels is coming to Peacock, with Seth MacFarlane's Fuzzy Door and co-showrunners Eric Heisserer and Chris Yost at the helm.

articles.title: The AI race is back on
articles.excerpt: Mark Zuckerberg at the Meta Connect developer conference. | Photo: Andrej Sokolow/dpa/picture alliance via Getty Images Last week, Anthropic and OpenAI looked like they had the AI race to themselves,…
articles.body: Mark Zuckerberg at the Meta Connect developer conference. | Photo: Andrej Sokolow/dpa/picture alliance via Getty Images Last week, Anthropic and OpenAI looked like they had the AI race to themselves, pulling ahead with increasingly powerful models that left their rivals in the dust. Google seemed hopelessly far behind, while Meta, despite spending billions to revive its floundering AI ambitions , had yet to establish itself as a serious contender. Even the latest models coming out of China , impressive as they were, appeared to be playing catch-up. Then, in the space of a few days, everything changed. Google and Meta both unveiled frontier models they claim can go toe to toe with the best from OpenAI and Anthropic.

articles.title: Anthropic warns small AI models could self-replicate through IoT devices
articles.excerpt: "Small weight-based replicators" could usher in a new generation of computer worms.
articles.body: AI company Anthropic is warning that advances in small AI models could soon usher in a new era of self-replicating malware that’s capable of infecting smart fridges, vacuum cleaners, and a wide range of other Internet of Things devices and is more resistant to takedown. By next year, smaller AI models may be able to autonomously self-replicate on all kinds of IoT devices, the company said. Eventually, the capability could enable computer worms, which propagate without requiring human interaction and are capable of infecting unfamiliar IoT devices. An experiment the company performed recently revealed significant challenges in bringing such an AI malware replicator to fruition, so the finding is necessarily tempered.
